prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: Across the five frames, a woman remains directly in front of the camera wearer at roughly 0.7–1.3 m, becoming slightly larger and nearer in the middle frames; her extended hand, the camera wearer’s hands, and the rectangular handheld objects are the nearest regions, approximately 0.2–0.6 m away and within arm’s reach. Chairs and refrigerated display cases lie behind her, mostly 2–5 m from the camera, while other people appear farther back in frames 2–5 at roughly 2–4 m and are partly occluded by her. The map makes foreground–background separation and the changing reach distance clearer than RGB, including the hands and objects projecting forward from the woman’s torso. Metric distances are only rough because monocular brightness is relative: the final frame makes the woman implausibly brighter than similar earlier views, and fine boundaries around hands, objects, and overlapping people are inconsistent.
descriptions.segmentation: The masks separate the central woman from chairs, display fixtures, tables, a laptop-like object, and additional people, showing the woman in front of most background objects and the camera wearer’s hands or held items overlapping her lower torso. The woman stays near the center or center-right across the strip, while background people shift through the gaps around her; several figures and objects are cut off at the left, right, and bottom borders or hidden behind foreground masks. This map makes instance extent and occlusion order easier to see than RGB, especially where dark clothing blends into the background, but it provides no dependable metric distance beyond apparent size and overlap. It is unreliable in class identity and continuity: display cases are repeatedly labelled “tv,” handheld items are fragmented or labelled as unrelated objects, chairs change shape or color between frames, and parts of people and hands are missing or merged.
descriptions.pose: The yellow skeletons show the central woman facing generally toward the camera wearer in frames 1–4, with her head above her shoulders and one or both arms extending forward into the space between them; the magenta hand landmarks in frames 2 and 4 place hands very close to the foreground interaction area, roughly within 0.3–0.7 m of the camera. Her arm configuration changes from a left-side bend in frame 1 to a more forward/central reach in frame 2, a lowered or inward configuration in frame 3, and a rightward extension in frame 4; frame 5 contains only a partial skeleton extending from the right edge, so body orientation there is uncertain. The pose map makes joint direction, limb reach, and hand proximity clearer than RGB, but it does not encode scene layout or reliable distances to chairs, displays, and background people. It is unreliable where bodies are occluded or cropped: legs and torsos are often absent, hand landmarks cluster into ambiguous blobs, background people are mostly undetected, and the final-frame skeleton does not align clearly with a complete visible person.
